en.name: Asafoetida
en.summary: Compounded asafoetida powder holds its aroma for roughly 6–12 months in a cool, dark cupboard. That is a reading rather than a published figure: extension guidance gives ground spices 6 months, compared with 1 to 2 years for whole spices, and hing powder is a resin cut with flour, so it sits between the two.
en.pantry: 6–12 months, and double-container it. Hing will scent every other spice in the cupboard, and a screw-top tin inside a sealed jar is the standard fix — this is not fussiness, it is the difference between cumin that tastes of cumin and cumin that tastes of hing. Cool, dark, dry, and away from the hob. The powder sold in India and abroad is compounded, meaning the resin is cut with wheat or rice flour and gum, so it is partly a flour product and stales faster than pure resin. Lump resin keeps for years but has to be ground or fried in oil before it releases anything.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for asafoetida. The cupboard is where it belongs, and the fridge introduces the two things a resin-and-flour powder does not want: humidity, which cakes it, and a confined space full of other smells, which cuts both ways given how strongly hing carries. If you keep it cold for any reason, let the sealed jar come fully to room temperature before opening it.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published either. Freezing would slow the aroma loss, but condensation on the powder every time the jar comes out would cake it, and the cupboard figure is adequate for a spice most people use a pinch of at a time. Buy the smallest tin you can find instead — that is the real answer.
en.thawing: Not applicable — asafoetida is a dry cupboard spice and should not be frozen.
spoilage: No smell at all when you open the tin, which means the aroma has gone.
Caking into hard lumps, from moisture getting into the container.
A dish that tastes of nothing where the hing should be.
Mould or a musty smell, which only happens in a tin that got damp.
tips: Keep the tin inside a sealed jar; hing will flavour every spice near it.
Buy the smallest container you can; a pinch at a time makes even a small tin last.
Fry it briefly in hot oil at the start of a dish — raw hing tastes harsh.
Lump resin keeps far longer than powder, but needs grinding or frying to do anything.

faq.a: Roughly 6–12 months in a cool, dark, airtight container. That is a judgement between the published figures for ground and whole spices, not a number published for hing itself.
It fades rather than spoils. Old hing is weak, not dangerous. Caking means moisture has got in, and only a genuinely damp tin will grow mould.

faq.q: Why does my whole spice cupboard smell of hing?
faq.a: Because a single container is not enough. Put the tin inside a sealed jar; the aroma travels through most lids.

zh.name: 阿魏
zh.summary: 調配過的阿魏粉，在陰涼避光的櫥櫃裡大約能維持 6～12 個月的香氣。這是一個判讀值，不是公布的數字：推廣單位的指引給研磨香料 6 個月，相較之下整粒香料是 1 到 2 年，而阿魏粉是樹脂混了麵粉，位置就落在兩者之間。
zh.pantry: 6～12 個月，而且請用兩層容器。阿魏會把櫥櫃裡每一種香料都染上味道，標準做法是「旋蓋鐵罐再放進密封玻璃罐」——這不是龜毛，這是「孜然吃起來像孜然」和「孜然吃起來像阿魏」的差別。陰涼、避光、乾燥，遠離爐台。市售的阿魏粉是調配品，也就是樹脂加了小麥粉或米粉與樹膠，所以它有一半是粉類製品，走味比純樹脂快。塊狀樹脂可以放好幾年，但必須磨碎或用油爆香才釋放得出東西。
zh.fridge: 阿魏沒有公布的冷藏期限。它該待的地方就是櫥櫃；冰箱會帶來這種「樹脂加粉」最不想要的兩件事：濕氣會讓它結塊，而一個封閉又充滿氣味的空間——考慮到阿魏的穿透力，這一點是雙向的麻煩。若因故冰過，請讓密封罐完全回到室溫再打開。
zh.freezer: 冷凍同樣沒有期限數據。冷凍確實能拖慢香氣流失，但每次拿出來粉上都會結露、進而結塊；而且對一種多數人每次只用一小撮的香料來說，櫥櫃的數字已經足夠。真正的答案是：買你找得到最小的那一罐。
zh.thawing: 不適用——阿魏是乾燥的櫥櫃香料，不應冷凍。
spoilage: 打開鐵罐完全聞不到味道，代表香氣已經跑光了。
結成硬塊，那是水氣跑進容器了。
該有阿魏味的菜嚐起來什麼都沒有。
長霉或有霉味——只有罐子真的受潮才會發生。
tips: 鐵罐再放進密封玻璃罐；阿魏會把附近每一種香料都調味。
買最小的容器；每次一小撮，再小的罐子都很耐用。
下鍋時用熱油爆香一下——生的阿魏味道很衝。
塊狀樹脂比粉耐放得多，但必須磨碎或爆香才有作用。

faq.a: 氣密容器放陰涼避光處，大約 6～12 個月。這是介於研磨香料與整粒香料公布數字之間的判斷，不是為阿魏本身公布的數字。
它是淡掉而不是腐敗。放久的阿魏是味道變弱，不是變危險。結塊代表受潮，只有真的潮濕的罐子才會長霉。

faq.q: 為什麼整個香料櫃都是阿魏味？
faq.a: 因為一層容器不夠。請把鐵罐再放進密封玻璃罐；那個氣味穿得過大多數蓋子。
